# InboxSieve

> InboxSieve is an AI filter for the messages from a website's contact form: it removes spam and sales pitches, scores real client requests 0-100, drafts a reply and pings you about the hot ones. For small agencies and service businesses. Self-serve, no sales call.

## What it does
- Takes inquiries from any form that can send an email (forwarding address) or a webhook (Webflow, Tally, Typeform, WPForms, Zapier, Make).
- Rule-based spam filter first, then an AI model scores each inquiry 0-100 against the customer's own business profile (services, ideal client, minimum budget, tone).
- Drafts a reply. A human always sends it from their own mail (copy, or open in Gmail/Outlook compose). InboxSieve never sends email as the customer.
- Hot-lead alerts by email to every seat and by Slack incoming webhook (Slack on paid plans).
- Inbox with score and stage filters, lead detail, pipeline (new, contacted, meeting, won, lost, spam).
- CSV export per brand, workspace deletion, 90-day purge of raw message bodies.

## Pricing (USD, sales tax/VAT added by Paddle where due)
- Free: $0, forever, no card needed. 1 brand, 1 source, 50 analyzed leads/month, 1 seat, email alerts (no Slack), CSV export.
- Paid: $4/month or $40/year (2 months free), one plan, cancel anytime. 1 brand, unlimited sources, 500 analyzed leads/month, 1 seat, Slack alerts.
- Sign-up starts on Free. The paid plan can be tried free for 14 days, no card needed; afterwards the workspace returns to Free unless you subscribe. Cancel any time. 14-day refund, no questions asked.
- A canceled subscription falls back to Free at the end of the paid period. Extra brands become read-only; nothing is deleted.
- Over the limit, leads are stored but not analyzed. Nothing is lost.
- Paddle.com is the merchant of record.

## Not included
- Sending replies from InboxSieve servers, Gmail/Outlook OAuth, CRM sync, auto-replies.

## Data
- The customer is the controller, InboxSieve the processor (GDPR/UK GDPR). A DPA is published.
- Sub-processors: Cloudflare, Groq, Brevo, Paddle.
- Lead data is never used to train AI models.
